title: Tesla Renames FSD to Tesla Assisted Driving to Win EU Approval
summary:
The branding for Tesla's autonomous software has been changed throughout Europe to align with regulatory expectations for driver-assistance systems. The product, previously known as "FSD (Supervised)," is now listed as "Tesla Assisted Driving" on the company's European websites and vehicle order pages in the UK. This nomenclature shift follows talks with Germany's Transport Ministry and is intended to facilitate EU-wide certification of the technology.

Germany's Transport Minister Steffen Bilger has urged the EU to approve the software, stating that it has the potential to make roads safer and support innovation. Bilger indicated that Germany might pursue its own separate approval route if discussions with the bloc fail, as the EU nears a vote on the system. Elon Musk responded to the minister's endorsement on social media on October 7, thanking the German official.

selectedTweets.text:
BREAKING: Germany’s transport minister pushes for Tesla FSD approval across Europe.

Speaking today at a Tagesspiegel Background conference in Berlin, Steffen Bilger said:

• He will push for Tesla FSD Supervised to reach drivers across the EU soon.

• He sees potential for FSD to make roads safer and wants to support innovation.

• Germany should explore its own approval route if EU talks fail.

• He will work to ensure that this system can be used throughout Europe soon.

📸 Lena Ganssmann / Tagesspiegel
